notices.clarification: The four resubmitted core files are byte-identical to published N780 and are not a new discovery. A separately preserved later wave adds exact fixed-degree partial-flag witness compilation, degree-promised model validation and persistent directed bad-item robust acquisition. Degree, fixed-tail/flag and corruption promises remain supplied; robust Monte Carlo wrong/UNKNOWN guarantees differ from the exact complete-class zero-semantic-error theorem. Current n16 and full-cube replays and final same-source RM controls are finite evidence, not universal advantage. The exact general capped bound remains D+(2T+2)P; its bare O(n^(d+1)) simplification needs fixed beta or a suitable growth restriction on log(1/beta). Degree-promised validation does not acquire the degree promise or contradict exact arbitrary-oracle recognition. See the new audit for guards, losses to controls, total source/bit costs and precise scope.

notices.clarification: The continuation minimal-monomial conjecture S_p<=m Pr(F!=0), equivalently W<=m k for fair bits, is exactly refuted: g(OR4(A)-OR4(B)) has m=k=30 and W=1024>900 in every nontrivial finite abelian group. Growing/tensor OR families rule out every fixed multiplier and give an all-group lower exponent above1.12197. A paired-literal binary-matroid construction raises the lower exponent to log2(1+sqrt(2)) for GF(2) and groups with a nonzero order-two element; no such per-group claim is made for odd-order groups. A separately proved group-safe dyadic/support-dependent repair survives, including an all-group m^2 fallback. These are proposal-cost bounds for the named mixture; factored OR/matroid examples have easy direct samplers after their representation is supplied. The decoder and arbitrary conditional-sampling problem remain intact. Historical open-conjecture wording is retained as history; a source paired-literal arithmetic typo is explicitly corrected in the new proof.

COMPARISON-ONLY ACQUISITION OF HIDDEN TRIANGULAR BOOLEAN DECODERS
13 October 2026. Internally proved and independently checked in this campaign.
Scientific novelty UNKNOWN. No civilization-enabling breakthrough established.

A comparison usually reveals much less than a numerical rank. For the class
below, translation pairs expose one entire coordinate function. Selecting the
most significant exposed coordinate before interpolating it makes full decoder
acquisition polynomial and avoids both rank enumeration and rare-prefix rejection.

Theorem and interface

Fix n>=2 and 1<=d<=n. Let u=Lx+c be an unknown invertible affine transformation
of F_2^n. Suppose the hidden rank, written most significant coordinate first, is

  Q(x)=(q_1(x),...,q_n(x)),
  q_i(x)=u_i+g_i(u_1,...,u_(i-1)),  deg(g_i)<=d.

The input includes n, d, this class promise, and exact chosen-pair access to
  C(x,y)=1[Q(x)<lex Q(y)].
The learner does not receive L, c, ranks, bit labels, g_i, target code, fiber
samplers, or translation directions. All random inputs below are fresh uniform
vectors. Addition is over F_2. Put

  M_d=sum_(j=0)^d binom(n,j), P=binom(n,2).

There is a Las Vegas learner acquiring an exact compact representation of
every q_i in its actual significance order (raw ANF expansion is separately
computable without further comparisons), with expected comparison count at most
  D+6P,  D=sum_(j=0)^d binom(n,j+1).
It terminates almost surely under the promise. With a cap
  T=ceil(log_2(P/beta)), 0<beta<1,
on the matching probes of each tournament pair, it instead returns either an
exact decoder or UNKNOWN. The probability of UNKNOWN is at most beta; its
worst comparison count is at most D+(2T+2)P. It never substitutes an
estimated coordinate on a capped failure. For fixed d>=2, this is O(n^(d+1))
comparisons, including the capped logarithmic term. In particular d=2 gives
expected O(n^3) and worst O(n^3+n^2 log(1/beta)) comparisons.

The acquired representation also provides an exact inverse rank map and an
exact uniform sampler for any requested rank prefix, without further queries.
